correctness.rationale: Conditionally unexposed deck entries are exchangeable, so adaptive visited labels are without-replacement draws. The coefficient polynomial counts exactly the t-subsets below the threshold. Fixed-t asymptotic counts arise from positive compositions minus pair collisions; intersections of distinct equalities lose two degrees of freedom. A uniform factorial majorant justifies termwise expectation limits, yielding the exact 7e/4 coefficient. A separate brute-force verifier checked 493231 shuffled decks, all reported tails and finite-n bias tests. Finite enumeration is not used to justify the infinite result.

value.rationale: The initiating extremal deck process has an explicitly motivated missing random-arrangement counterpart. The complete finite population law is computable for arbitrary multiplicity, and the nontrivial 7e/4 correction quantifies how forced distinctness and integer thresholds alter the classical e-limit. The finite correction is not a routine restatement of the iid theorem; its collision count and uniform asymptotic interchange are essential. No general large-m theory or larger downstream theorem is claimed.
